orders.label: When it was written
orders.note: Each text stands in the century it was written, dated as its sources word it.
orders.line: Every text on the shelf, standing in the century it was written. Pull one out to read it.

books.title: The Abhidharma Mahāvibhāṣā
books.author: The five hundred arhats of Kashmir, translated into Chinese by Xuanzang
books.premise: The Sarvāstivāda school's great commentary on Kātyāyanīputra's Jñānaprasthāna: two hundred fascicles weighing every question of the Abhidharma, the Kashmir masters against the Dārṣṭāntikas, the Vātsīputrīyas and the other schools, and the positions Vasubandhu's Abhidharmakośa later summarized and argued with.

written.label: 150–250 CE
written.evidence: Potter, ed., Abhidharma Buddhism to 150 A.D. (1996), p. 112: compiled about 150 CE; Keown, A Dictionary of Buddhism (Oxford, 2003), "Mahāvibhāṣā": not at Kaniṣka I's council, since the text names the "former king Kaniṣka", but probably the 3rd century CE in Gandhāra under Kaniṣka II, who reigned about 232–247 CE (Wikipedia, "Kanishka II"); translated into Chinese by Xuanzang in 656–659 CE (Williams, Kośa Symposium 2022, table of Xuanzang's Abhidharma translations: T1545, 656–59)

editions.cite: Takakusu Junjirō 高楠順次郎 and Watanabe Kaigyoku 渡邊海旭, eds. *Taishō shinshū daizōkyō* 大正新脩大藏經. Vol. 27, no. 1545. Tokyo: Taishō Issaikyō Kankōkai, 1924–1934.

length.evidence: Taishō vol. 27, pp. 1a–1004a: 1,004 pages of three registers, each 29 columns of 17 characters, about 1,480 characters a page at the most, so about 7,400 a fascicle; counted exactly once the text is established

books.title: The Long Discourses, with the Sumaṅgalavilāsinī
books.author: The Dīgha Nikāya, with Buddhaghosa's commentary
books.premise: The thirty-four long discourses of the Dīgha Nikāya, each with Buddhaghosa's commentary on it, the Sumaṅgalavilāsinī, which has almost no English.

written.label: 412–450 CE
written.evidence: Dated by its commentary, which Buddhaghosa wrote at the Mahāvihāra in Anurādhapura: he arrived in the reign of King Mahānāma, 412–434 CE (Ñāṇamoli, The Path of Purification, 1999, p. xxvi), and is dated about 370–450 CE (von Hinüber, A Handbook of Pāli Literature, 1996, p. 103), both by Wikipedia, "Buddhaghosa"; the suttas are older, and the book's own /design may date it by them

books.title: The Middle-Length Discourses, with the Papañcasūdanī
books.author: The Majjhima Nikāya, with Buddhaghosa's commentary
books.premise: The 152 middle-length discourses of the Majjhima Nikāya, each with Buddhaghosa's commentary on it, the Papañcasūdanī.

written.label: 412–450 CE
written.evidence: Dated by its commentary, which Buddhaghosa wrote at the Mahāvihāra in Anurādhapura: he arrived in the reign of King Mahānāma, 412–434 CE (Ñāṇamoli, The Path of Purification, 1999, p. xxvi), and is dated about 370–450 CE (von Hinüber, A Handbook of Pāli Literature, 1996, p. 103), both by Wikipedia, "Buddhaghosa"; the suttas are older, and the book's own /design may date it by them

books.title: The Life of Tilopa
books.author: Marpa Chökyi Lodrö
books.premise: The earliest life of the mahāsiddha Tilopa, the short text Marpa wrote for his son Darma Dode, kept in the Rechung aural lineage collection.

written.label: 1012–1097 CE
written.evidence: Written by Marpa Chökyi Lodrö for his son Darma Dode: its colophon, "dpal gro bo lung gi dgon par / sras mdo sde'i don du yi ger bkod pa rdzogs so", written at Drowolung for his son Dode (the Apho Rinpoche manuscript, folio 11b, BDRC W24891 image 44); so within Marpa's life, 1012–1097 (Wikipedia, "Marpa Lotsawa")

editions.editor: Apho Rinpoche's manuscript, compiled by Byang chub bzang po
editions.cite: Bde mchog mkha' 'gro snyan rgyud (Ras chung snyan rgyud), New Delhi, 1973, volume 1, pages 7–28: the manuscript compiled by Byang chub bzang po in the library of Apho Rinpoche, section Kha, folios 1a–11b, BDRC W24891 (I6068, images 23–44), open access, established from its leaves, a published transliteration of the same leaves consulted (Torricelli and Naga, Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, 1995). Read beside other tellings of the life scanned at BDRC: W3CN15304 (I3CN15860, folios 4b–31a), and W30124, the Jatang manuscript (I5884, pages 22–43) and the Drakar manuscript (I5885, pages 97–118)

length.evidence: Syllables counted between the tshegs of the established Tibetan, writing/buddhism/books/marpas-life-of-tilopa/work/tilopa-tibetan.md, 20 October 2026, 1:09pm: all twenty-four pages of the transliteration

books.title: Tāranātha's Seven Lineages
books.author: Tāranātha, translated through Albert Grünwedel's German of 1914
books.premise: The bKa' babs bdun ldan: the lives of the Indian siddhas of seven tantric lineages, Tilopa and Nāropa among them, as Tāranātha gathered them in his twenty-sixth year.

written.label: 1600 CE
written.evidence: The colophon, Grünwedel 1914, printed p. 154: "vollbracht von Tāranātha in seinem fast sechsundzwanzigsten Jahre"; Tāranātha was born in 1575 (Wikipedia, "Tāranātha"; the Penn catalog record of Templeman's translation, "1575-1634"), so 1600 CE

editions.cite: Grünwedel, Albert, trans. *Tāranātha's Edelsteinmine, das Buch von den Vermittlern der sieben Inspirationen*. Bibliotheca Buddhica 18. Petrograd, 1914.

books.title: The Treasury of Precious Instructions
books.author: Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, compiler
books.premise: The gdams ngag mdzod: eighteen volumes of the practice instructions of the eight lineages of Tibetan Buddhism, gathered by Jamgön Kongtrul from the Indian siddhas to his own day.

written.label: 1870–1899 CE
written.evidence: Compiled in the 1870s, by the publisher's dating of the first carving at Palpung in the DNZ catalog's "Survey of the gdams ngag mdzod" (about.sakyaresearch.org, source S5810), and closed by Kongtrul's death in 1899
